source.title: Construct the Minimum Bitwise Array II

teaching.hint: What does adding one do to the low-order run of bits before the OR is taken?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Adding one flips the trailing ones and first zero, so a valid predecessor is obtained by clearing one bit in the target's trailing ones.
solution_outline.approach: For each target, locate its trailing run of set bits. If absent, return -1; otherwise clear the highest bit in that run to get the smallest predecessor.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each eligible cleared bit produces a predecessor whose lowest zero is exactly that bit, so OR with its successor restores the target.
solution_outline.correctness: The carry pattern proves all valid predecessors come from those positions. Clearing the highest eligible bit subtracts the most and therefore minimizes the result.
solution_outline.complexity: O(q log M) time for q values bounded by M and O(1) extra space apart from output.
solution_outline.pitfall: Clearing the lowest set bit is valid for odd targets but may not give the minimum.

common_wrong_turns: Return x-1 for every odd x
source_fidelity_notes: The prime input guarantee and independent minimization per index remain explicit.
